description: A family-aware diagnostic adapter for Self-EvolveRec that inspects the trained HSTU recommender through the host ModelView interface. It returns measured metrics with explicit definitions and builds an interpretation prompt grounded in those measurements.
motivation: Make model diagnosis useful for iterative improvement while preserving benchmark comparability, HSTU compatibility, and the distinction between observable interaction patterns and unavailable user traits.
implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model as the actual trained network and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Run probes in evaluation mode without gradients, restoring the previous training mode afterward. Mask padding and invalid targets; for sequence readout, use the final nonpadding position in left-padded histories. Possible probes include positive–negative score margins, representation norms, and recommendation coverage, each reported with its definition, sample count, and limitations. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps; mark unavailable attributes as unobserved. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category. Keep one independently trained HSTU checkpoint per category, consistent with the embedded predictor. Model selection remains the host's macro validation HR@10 across all four categories.
pseudocode:
DiagnosisProbe(view, device):
  run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save model training state; enter eval mode and no_grad
    for (_, sequence, positive, negative) in train_loader:
      features = view.log2feats(sequence)
      identify valid nonpadding positions and targets
      score positives and negatives using view.predict_score
      accumulate defined diagnostic measurements over valid entries
    restore model training state
    return {metrics: aggregated measurements, metric_definitions: definitions and limitations}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
  include measured metrics and their definitions
  request evidence-grounded interpretations and HSTU-compatible hypotheses
  distinguish observations from hypotheses and unavailable information
  preserve single-model training and fixed benchmark constraints

originality.positive: Combines explicit diagnostic definitions with a family-specific compatibility contract and strict observability constraints.
originality.negative: Primarily an integration and measurement protocol rather than a new recommendation algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Could support more reliable architecture and optimization experiments by linking proposed changes to measurable model behavior.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic improvements do not establish ranking improvements; proposals still require validation under the fixed evaluator.

code_difficulty.positive: The required interfaces are narrow, and most probes can reuse existing model features and scoring methods.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct padding masks, feature shapes, full-catalog scoring, and checkpoint–predictor consistency require careful implementation.
